title: Pro-rate billing and quotas for mid-stream model fallbacks
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Problem: When the serving layer triggers an automatic fallback mid-stream (for example, capacity overflow on model-A -> fallback to model-B), we currently attribute all generated tokens to the model that finishes the request or to the final backend that acknowledged the stream. This leads to incorrect per-model billing, quota enforcement, and misleading cost dashboards. Edge cases include: (1) cached prefix tokens that are replayed by the fallback backend, (2) resumed streams or retry-after-failure where both backends claim token counts, (3) per-model quotas and rate limits being hit incorrectly after a partial switch, and (4) function-calling / tool invocation where tool responses are stitched and cause origin confusion. Goal: implement atomic, pro-rated token attribution and quota enforcement for mid-stream model switches so that tokens produced before the switch are billed/charged against the origin model and tokens after the switch are billed against the fallback model. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and monitoring changes across the metering pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Token attribution is recorded with a MODEL_SWITCH marker event referencing the sequence offset and origin model id for all mid-stream switches.
Billing aggregator charges tokens to the model that actually generated them (pre-switch vs post-switch) in the billing reports for 99.9% of test cases in the harness.
No double-counting of tokens across backends when streams are resumed or retried; reconciliation tests validate idempotency.
Per-model and org-level quotas respect mid-stream attribution (example: if model-A quota exhausted mid-stream and fallback to model-B occurs, model-A quota usage equals tokens before switch).
Latency/throughput regressions are within acceptable range (<1.5% P99 increase) after instrumentation changes.
Dashboards expose a new 'mid-stream-fallback' meter and a fallout rate metric (switches per 10k streams)
Automated E2E test scenarios for cached-prefix, retry, multiplexed sessions, and function-calling flows added to CI and passing.
tasks: Design: define MODEL_SWITCH event schema and sequence-offset attribution semantics (eng + billing review)
Runtime: emit MODEL_SWITCH marker at switch boundary with origin_model_id, new_model_id, switch_offset, reason_code
Metering pipeline: extend token-aggregator to assign origin_id per token chunk based on markers
Billing: update invoice generator to accept per-token origin_id and produce per-model billing lines
Quota enforcement: ensure quota checks consult origin attribution for pre-switch credits and only decrement fallback model for post-switch tokens
Testing: build synthetic harness with scenarios (prefix cache replay, resume after reconnect, retry with different backend, multiplexed streams)
Observability: add dashboards and alerts for mid-stream switches, and add reconciliation job to detect anomalous double-count rates
Docs: update API docs explaining mid-stream attribution implications for quota and billing
comments: 2025-11-03 - Aisha Kaur: Initial write-up. Observed discrepancy in November billing run for org X where 12% of tokens were attributed to fallback model despite primary producing the prefix. Filing design to avoid surprises to customers.

2025-11-04 - Benji Morales: Added runtime implementation notes — we can emit MODEL_SWITCH as part of the stream control plane event. Need to coordinate with proxy retry behavior to avoid losing marker on reconnect.

2025-11-05 - Priya Desai (Billing): We must ensure backwards-compatible billing rows for customers on legacy reporting. Billing pipeline can accept origin_id but fallback to legacy behavior if absent.
2025-11-07 - Miguel Ortiz (SRE): Watch for increased cardinality in metrics. Suggest sampling switch events in high-volume tenants and add summary counters to avoid Grafana overload.

2025-11-10 - Design review notes: Agreed to add explicit sequence offsets and a hermetic reconciliation job that replays raw events and validates invoices. Security review not required for metadata only, but ensure no PII in markers.
notes: Implementation will add a small wire protocol change (marker event) between runtime and metering. Compatibility strategy: runtime emits marker optionally; metering treats missing marker as 'no mid-stream switch'. We'll schedule a canary rollout to Dedicated and Hosted regions separately. Expect coordination with console and billing teams for roll-forward of invoice format.
